title: Honey Garlic Chicken
subtitle: Sticky pan-fried chicken thighs in a sweet garlic glaze
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs get a quick sear then finish in a glossy honey, garlic and soy glaze. A small spoon of cornflour thickens the sauce in the pan. The whole thing is on the table in 30 minutes.
sourceNotes: Honey garlic chicken is a staple of American home cooking with roots in Chinese-American restaurant sauces. The sticky pan-glaze method grew popular as a fast weeknight alternative to full stir-fries.

content.text: Dry the chicken well before it hits the pan so it sears rather than steams. The sauce thickens fast at the end so keep the heat moderate and stir constantly.
Pat the chicken dry and season well with salt and pepper. Mix the honey, soy, rice vinegar and garlic together in a small bowl.
Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the chicken smooth-side down and cook for 6 to 7 minutes without moving.
Flip and cook for a further 5 minutes until cooked through. Remove to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the ginger to the pan and cook for 30 seconds. Pour in the sauce mixture and bubble for 1 minute.
Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook, stirring, until the sauce is thick and glossy, about 1 minute.
Return the chicken to the pan and turn to coat in the glaze. Serve over rice.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thin and watery.
items.cause: Cornflour slurry was not fully mixed or added too early.
items.fix: Stir slurry well and add only after sauce bubbles.

items.symptom: Chicken is pale and not seared.
items.cause: The pan was not hot enough or chicken was wet.
items.fix: Pat chicken very dry and heat oil until it shimmers.
